title: Lesson 01 - Introduction to Corporate Finance
description: A challenging assessment of financial systems, corporate finance decisions, value creation, cash flows, shareholder wealth maximization, and agency problems.
subject: FIN2372 - Advanced Corporate Finance

questions.question: A household earns more cash income than it spends on consumption and real investment during the year. It uses the excess funds to purchase newly issued corporate bonds. Which interpretation is most accurate?
options: The household is a deficit spending unit purchasing a real asset
The household is a surplus spending unit supplying loanable funds
The household is a financial intermediary transforming financial claims
The household is a deficit spending unit issuing a financial liability
questions.answer: The household is a surplus spending unit supplying loanable funds
questions.rationale: A unit whose income exceeds expenditure is a surplus spending unit and can supply its excess funds to deficit spending units by purchasing financial assets.

questions.question: A manufacturing company requires additional funds to construct a new factory and issues securities to investors. From the perspective of the financial system, which description best applies to the company?
options: It is a surplus spending unit because it is creating productive assets
It is a financial intermediary because it connects investment with financing
It is a deficit spending unit because its planned expenditure exceeds available internal funds
It is a financial investor because the factory is expected to generate future returns
questions.answer: It is a deficit spending unit because its planned expenditure exceeds available internal funds
questions.rationale: A deficit spending unit requires external financing when its planned expenditures exceed available funds and may obtain those funds by issuing securities.

questions.question: An investor purchases a newly issued bond directly from a company. Which statement best describes the financial claim created by this transaction?
options: The bond is an asset to both the investor and the issuing company
The bond is a liability to the investor and an asset to the issuing company
The bond is a financial asset to the investor and an offsetting liability to the company
The bond becomes a real asset because the proceeds may finance physical investment
questions.answer: The bond is a financial asset to the investor and an offsetting liability to the company
questions.rationale: Every financial asset held by one economic unit corresponds to an offsetting financial liability of another economic unit.

questions.question: Suppose investors sell existing shares to one another without the issuing company receiving any new funds. What is the most important economic contribution of this activity?
options: It directly finances new capital expenditure undertaken by the issuing company
It creates additional accounting profits for the company whose shares are traded
It converts the company from a deficit spending unit into a surplus spending unit
It provides liquidity by allowing existing financial claims to be exchanged
questions.answer: It provides liquidity by allowing existing financial claims to be exchanged
questions.rationale: Trading existing securities in secondary markets primarily provides liquidity rather than directly supplying new financing to the original issuer.

questions.question: A company must choose between two projects with identical expected total cash inflows, but one project generates most of its cash earlier. Why can the projects have different values?
options: Financial value depends on both the amount and timing of expected cash flows
Earlier cash flows automatically eliminate all uncertainty associated with investment
Later cash flows are excluded from corporate finance analysis until they are received
Accounting standards require earlier cash flows to be reported as additional equity
questions.answer: Financial value depends on both the amount and timing of expected cash flows
questions.rationale: Finance recognizes that costs and benefits occur over time, making the timing as well as the amount of future cash flows relevant to value.

questions.question: Which decision would most directly fall within the capital budgeting responsibility of a financial manager?
options: Choosing the proportion of long term borrowing relative to shareholder financing
Determining whether a new production facility will generate sufficient value
Deciding how much cash should be retained for immediate supplier payments
Selecting the accounting method used to report depreciation expenses
questions.answer: Determining whether a new production facility will generate sufficient value
questions.rationale: Capital budgeting concerns the evaluation and selection of long term investments in assets and projects.

questions.question: A company has already selected a profitable expansion project and must now decide whether to finance it primarily through long term debt or new equity. Which corporate finance decision is being made?
options: Capital budgeting
Liquidity transformation
Capital structure
Net working capital management
questions.answer: Capital structure
questions.rationale: Capital structure decisions determine the mix of financing sources, particularly debt and equity, used by a firm.

questions.question: A profitable company repeatedly struggles to pay suppliers because excessive funds are tied up in inventory and customer receivables. Which financial management area is most directly responsible for addressing the problem?
options: Capital structure management
Net working capital management
Long term capital budgeting
Securities market regulation
questions.answer: Net working capital management
questions.rationale: Net working capital management focuses on short term assets and liabilities and the firm's ability to support daily operations and meet short term obligations.

questions.question: Which situation best demonstrates why maximizing accounting profit may fail to maximize shareholder wealth?
options: A project increases reported profit but generates uncertain cash flows far into the future
A project increases both immediate cash flow and the market value of the company's shares
A company replaces expensive borrowing with a cheaper source of financing
A company rejects a project whose expected benefits are lower than its economic costs
questions.answer: A project increases reported profit but generates uncertain cash flows far into the future
questions.rationale: Profit alone does not adequately capture the timing and risk of future benefits, both of which affect shareholder wealth.

questions.question: A financial manager rejects a project that would increase next year's accounting profit because the project's risk and delayed cash flows are expected to reduce the current market value of the company. Which objective is the manager applying?
options: Revenue maximization
Shareholder wealth maximization
Market share maximization
Accounting profit maximization
questions.answer: Shareholder wealth maximization
questions.rationale: Shareholder wealth maximization focuses on decisions that increase the current value of the firm's stock rather than merely increasing reported profit.

questions.question: A company makes a large credit sale near the end of its financial year, records the revenue immediately, but will collect the customer payment several months later. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: The transaction can increase accounting income before producing an equivalent cash inflow
The transaction immediately increases both accounting income and operating cash by equal amounts
The transaction increases cash flow immediately but cannot affect accounting income until collection
The transaction has no financial significance until the customer settles the outstanding balance
questions.answer: The transaction can increase accounting income before producing an equivalent cash inflow
questions.rationale: Accounting income and cash flow can differ because revenue may be recognized before the related cash is actually collected.

questions.question: Which condition most strongly indicates that a firm is creating economic value through its financing and investment activities?
options: The firm continuously increases the number of securities it issues
The firm reports higher revenue regardless of the capital required to generate it
The return generated on invested capital exceeds the cost of obtaining that capital
The firm's total assets increase faster than its annual accounting depreciation
questions.answer: The return generated on invested capital exceeds the cost of obtaining that capital
questions.rationale: Value is created when the return generated by invested capital exceeds the cost of the capital used to finance the investment.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the value creation perspective of finance described in the lesson?
options: Financial wealth creates real productive assets independently of business investment
Value originates in productive real assets and is transmitted through financial claims held by investors
Value is created primarily through repeated trading of existing securities between investors
Financial contracting creates wealth by eliminating the uncertainty associated with real investments
questions.answer: Value originates in productive real assets and is transmitted through financial claims held by investors
questions.rationale: The value creation perspective explains that value is generated by productive real assets and transmitted into the financial securities issued against the business.

questions.question: An investor wants an asset that can be sold quickly without suffering a substantial loss caused by the need to find a buyer. Which property of a financial asset is the investor primarily concerned with?
options: Expected return
Credit exposure
Liquidity
Market maturity
questions.answer: Liquidity
questions.rationale: Liquidity concerns the ability to sell an asset quickly without suffering a significant loss or undertaking a costly search for a buyer.

questions.question: Two securities offer the same expected return, but one has a substantially greater probability that the issuer will fail to make promised payments. Which property most clearly distinguishes the securities?
options: Credit risk
Liquidity preference
Financial intermediation
Capital structure
questions.answer: Credit risk
questions.rationale: Credit risk concerns the possibility that an issuer or borrower will fail to meet promised financial obligations.

questions.question: Which transaction best represents indirect rather than direct financing?
options: A household purchases newly issued corporate shares through a broker
An investor buys an existing government security from another investor
A company sells newly issued bonds directly to institutional investors
A household deposits funds with a bank that subsequently lends to a business
questions.answer: A household deposits funds with a bank that subsequently lends to a business
questions.rationale: Indirect financing occurs when a financial intermediary stands between surplus and deficit units and issues its own claims while acquiring claims issued by borrowers.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately distinguishes a broker or dealer from a financial intermediary in the flow of funds?
options: A broker or dealer facilitates direct financing, while an intermediary participates in indirect financing
A broker or dealer creates only real assets, while an intermediary creates only tangible assets
A broker or dealer can serve only deficit units, while an intermediary can serve only surplus units
A broker or dealer eliminates financial claims, while an intermediary eliminates financial liabilities
questions.answer: A broker or dealer facilitates direct financing, while an intermediary participates in indirect financing
questions.rationale: Brokers and dealers facilitate transactions involving direct financial claims, whereas intermediaries transform claims in the indirect financing process.

questions.question: A business experiencing a financing deficit could restore balance between its cash inflows and outflows in several ways. Which action is most consistent with the behavior of a deficit spending unit?
options: Purchasing additional financial assets using excess current income
Issuing financial liabilities to obtain funds from the financial sector
Increasing money balances while simultaneously reducing all borrowing
Supplying additional loanable funds to other deficit spending units
questions.answer: Issuing financial liabilities to obtain funds from the financial sector
questions.rationale: A deficit spending unit can obtain funds by issuing financial liabilities, reducing money balances, or selling previously acquired financial assets.

questions.question: Which statement about financial claims is logically required for the financial system as a whole?
options: Total financial assets must exceed total financial liabilities whenever firms invest
Every financial liability must eventually be converted into a tangible real asset
Total financial receivables must correspond to total financial payables
Financial assets can exist without an offsetting obligation when traded in secondary markets
questions.answer: Total financial receivables must correspond to total financial payables
questions.rationale: A financial asset for one party represents a corresponding financial liability for another, so aggregate receivables and payables must correspond.

questions.question: Which of the following is the strongest example of an intangible asset rather than a tangible real asset or a financial asset?
options: A listed ordinary share
A production machine
A legally protected patent
A government debt security
questions.answer: A legally protected patent
questions.rationale: A patent is an intangible asset whose value arises from legal rights rather than physical properties or a financial claim against another economic unit.

questions.question: A company raises funds by issuing new shares and invests the proceeds in productive machinery. Which statement best describes the transformation involved?
options: The company transforms financial wealth obtained from investors into productive real assets
The company transforms machinery into a financial liability held by its suppliers
The investors acquire ownership of the machinery as their direct personal real asset
The issuance eliminates the distinction between real assets and financial claims
questions.answer: The company transforms financial wealth obtained from investors into productive real assets
questions.rationale: Corporate finance connects financial claims supplied by investors with investment in real business assets that are expected to create value.

questions.question: Which scenario most clearly represents a potential agency problem between shareholders and managers?
options: Managers reject a negative value project despite its potential to increase company size
Managers undertake an expansion mainly to increase their prestige despite reducing shareholder value
Managers close a persistently unprofitable division to redirect resources toward better investments
Managers adopt performance targets that directly reward increases in long term shareholder value
questions.answer: Managers undertake an expansion mainly to increase their prestige despite reducing shareholder value
questions.rationale: An agency problem arises when managers pursue personal objectives that conflict with the goal of maximizing shareholder wealth.

questions.question: A board redesigns executive compensation so that a significant portion of management rewards depends on sustained increases in shareholder value. What is the primary purpose of this policy?
options: To eliminate the need for shareholders to provide capital
To align managerial incentives more closely with shareholder objectives
To convert managers from agents into legal owners of all company assets
To prevent financial markets from influencing corporate decision making
questions.answer: To align managerial incentives more closely with shareholder objectives
questions.rationale: Performance related managerial compensation can reduce agency conflicts by making managers benefit when shareholder wealth increases.

questions.question: Why can widely dispersed ownership increase the potential importance of corporate governance mechanisms?
options: Dispersed shareholders may individually have limited ability to monitor management effectively
Dispersed ownership automatically prevents managers from controlling corporate resources
Dispersed shareholders are legally prohibited from voting on matters affecting management
Dispersed ownership converts all shareholder claims into short term corporate liabilities
questions.answer: Dispersed shareholders may individually have limited ability to monitor management effectively
questions.rationale: When ownership is widely dispersed, management may effectively control the firm because individual shareholders have weaker incentives and ability to exercise direct control.

questions.question: Which action is most clearly an agency cost intended to reduce conflicts between managers and shareholders?
options: Paying for an independent audit that monitors managerial reporting
Purchasing a profitable machine that increases future operating cash flows
Accepting a project that creates more value than the capital invested
Repaying a loan according to the original contractual repayment schedule
questions.answer: Paying for an independent audit that monitors managerial reporting
questions.rationale: Monitoring expenditures such as independent audit costs can arise because shareholders need mechanisms to reduce or control agency conflicts.

questions.question: Which combination most directly influences whether managers are likely to act in shareholders' best interests according to the agency framework discussed in the lesson?
options: The number of products sold and the age of the company
The level of inventory and the maturity of outstanding debt
The alignment of managerial goals and the possibility of replacing ineffective managers
The size of the accounting department and the frequency of financial reporting
questions.answer: The alignment of managerial goals and the possibility of replacing ineffective managers
questions.rationale: Managerial behavior is influenced by how closely management incentives align with shareholder objectives and whether control mechanisms allow poorly performing managers to be replaced.

questions.question: A firm reports a large increase in annual accounting profit, but its share price falls after investors learn that the profit resulted from highly risky projects with uncertain distant cash flows. Which conclusion is most consistent with corporate finance principles?
options: The market reaction is inconsistent because higher accounting profit must increase shareholder wealth
The market reaction can be rational because value depends on risk, timing, and expected cash flows
The market reaction proves that accounting information has no relevance to financial decisions
The market reaction means that shareholders always prefer immediate dividends to profitable investment
questions.answer: The market reaction can be rational because value depends on risk, timing, and expected cash flows
questions.rationale: Shareholder wealth reflects expected future cash flows together with their timing and uncertainty, not accounting profit alone.

questions.question: A firm generates cash from its operating assets, pays taxes, reinvests part of the remaining cash, and distributes the balance to debt and equity investors. Which principle best determines whether the overall financial process creates value for investors?
options: The firm must distribute every operating cash flow immediately rather than retain funds
The firm must ensure that accounting revenue always exceeds the book value of assets
The firm must generate cash flows sufficient to compensate providers of capital for the funds committed
The firm must finance all productive assets using internally generated cash rather than external securities
questions.answer: The firm must generate cash flows sufficient to compensate providers of capital for the funds committed
questions.rationale: The financial manager seeks to create value by ensuring that the firm's investments generate more value and cash than the resources required to finance them.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why finance cannot be treated simply as the process of raising money?
options: Finance also examines how scarce resources are allocated over time under uncertainty
Finance is concerned exclusively with recording historical transactions after they occur
Finance excludes investment decisions because these belong entirely to accounting
Finance studies only government borrowing and the regulation of financial institutions
questions.answer: Finance also examines how scarce resources are allocated over time under uncertainty
questions.rationale: Finance is broader than fundraising because it examines resource allocation across time while considering uncertain future costs and benefits.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes the relationship between finance and accounting information?
options: Finance replaces accounting because historical information has no decision making value
Finance uses accounting information as an input but applies analytical principles to financial decisions
Finance and accounting are identical because both focus exclusively on reported profit
Finance produces accounting information while accounting determines the market value of securities
questions.answer: Finance uses accounting information as an input but applies analytical principles to financial decisions
questions.rationale: Finance draws on accounting information but uses analytical and economic principles to evaluate decisions involving investment, financing, risk, and value.

questions.question: Which choice correctly distinguishes corporate finance from the investment area of finance?
options: Corporate finance studies how firms raise and use funds, while investment studies securities and portfolio decisions
Corporate finance studies only short term borrowing, while investment studies all long term financing decisions
Corporate finance focuses on financial markets, while investment focuses exclusively on physical business assets
Corporate finance evaluates personal securities, while investment determines corporate capital structures
questions.answer: Corporate finance studies how firms raise and use funds, while investment studies securities and portfolio decisions
questions.rationale: Corporate finance focuses on the financial decisions of firms, whereas the investment field focuses on securities markets and the evaluation and management of investments.

questions.question: A government spends substantially more than its current revenues and finances the difference by issuing government securities purchased by households. Which classification best describes the two parties in this transaction?
options: The government is the surplus unit and households are the deficit units
Both the government and households are deficit units because securities are involved
The government is the deficit unit and households are acting as surplus units
Both parties are surplus units because financial assets are created by the transaction
questions.answer: The government is the deficit unit and households are acting as surplus units
questions.rationale: Governments are commonly deficit spending units when expenditure exceeds income, while households commonly supply excess funds by purchasing financial claims.

questions.question: An investor buys shares of an existing listed company from another investor on a stock exchange. Which statement best describes the transaction?
options: The issuing company receives new financing and creates a new real asset
The transaction transfers an existing financial claim and contributes primarily to market liquidity
The selling investor becomes a deficit spending unit solely because the shares were sold
The transaction eliminates the corresponding equity claim from the company's capital structure
questions.answer: The transaction transfers an existing financial claim and contributes primarily to market liquidity
questions.rationale: Secondary market transactions transfer existing securities between investors and enhance liquidity without directly providing new funds to the issuing company.

questions.question: A manager must choose between Project A, which increases company size and managerial status but reduces the current value of the firm's shares, and Project B, which is smaller but increases share value. Under the stated goal of financial management, which decision is appropriate?
options: Choose Project A because larger firms necessarily create greater shareholder wealth
Choose Project A because managerial control is the primary objective of corporate finance
Choose Project B because increasing the current value of existing stock is the relevant objective
Choose either project because shareholder wealth is independent of managerial investment decisions
questions.answer: Choose Project B because increasing the current value of existing stock is the relevant objective
questions.rationale: The goal of financial management is to maximize the current value of existing stock, so the project that increases shareholder value should be preferred.

questions.question: A financial manager simultaneously evaluates a factory expansion, determines how much debt should finance it, and establishes policies for inventory and short term obligations. Which interpretation is most accurate?
options: The manager is addressing investment, financing, and net working capital decisions that jointly influence firm value
The manager is performing three accounting functions that have no direct connection with shareholder wealth
The manager is addressing only capital budgeting because every decision ultimately relates to investment
The manager is performing financial intermediation by transferring funds between independent surplus units
questions.answer: The manager is addressing investment, financing, and net working capital decisions that jointly influence firm value
questions.rationale: Corporate finance centers on capital budgeting, capital structure, and net working capital management, with all three contributing to the financial manager's value creation responsibility.
